=={{header|Cxc}}==

Cxc has no <code>while</code> loop; iteration folds into the atom lifecycle. The <code>main</code> atom carries a counter field <code>n</code>, enters <code>running</code>, and self-sends <code>tick</code>. Each tick reads the <code>word_for</code> observation, prints it, advances <code>n</code> via the <code>=&gt;</code> transition arrow, and self-sends until the terminal guard <code>n &gt; 100</code> fires the arm whose target is <code>end</code>.

The <code>word_for</code> observation derives the output by composition rather than by a lookup table: multiples of 3 produce <code>"Fizz"</code>, multiples of 5 produce <code>"Buzz"</code>, and their concatenation covers multiples of 15 without a special case. <code>combined.not_empty() ?? n.to_string()</code> reads as "value, else default" — <code>.not_empty()</code> returns the string when it has content, or <code>nil</code> when empty, and the <code>??</code> nil-coalesce falls through to the number.

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
def main:
    n: Int! = 1

    word_for :- String!
        fizz     :- ||: n % 3 == 0 : "Fizz" |?: ""
        buzz     :- ||: n % 5 == 0 : "Buzz" |?: ""
        combined :- fizz + buzz
        combined.not_empty() ?? n.to_string()

    -> running
        then: self :> tick

    running <: tick:
        |: n > 100 -> end
        |: else    -> running
            then:
                print(self.word_for)
                n => n + 1
                self :> tick
</syntaxhighlight>

Outer observations (declared on an atom or record) and inner bindings (declared inside an observation body) share one shape: <code>name :- expression</code>. The nested form reuses the outer glyph, so <code>fizz :- "Fizz"</code> at the inner position reads the same way as <code>word_for :- String!</code> at the outer position — a named pure derivation over the surrounding state.

Inside an observation, <code>||: guard : body</code> is an expression-position multi-arm dispatch: the first arm whose guard holds yields its body value, and the closing <code>|?: body</code> covers the no-match case. The two glyphs together replace <code>if</code> / <code>else if</code> / <code>else</code>; cxc has no <code>if</code> expression at v1.0.

The receive-side uses a grouped shape: <code>running &lt;: tick:</code> opens the group, and each arm hangs beneath as <code>|: guard -&gt; target</code>. First-match dispatch in source order fires the terminal arm when <code>n &gt; 100</code> holds, and the <code>|: else</code> fall-through arm runs the self-loop body otherwise. <code>:&gt;</code> is an asynchronous self-send that enqueues the next <code>tick</code> on the atom's own serial dispatch queue.
